title: Victorian pool permit drawings, build time limits and stop-and-report steps
audience: Pool builders, installers, supervisors and service workers on pool projects in Victoria. Permit and registration rules are Victorian. Builder registration is a licence-type requirement; this lesson does not grant it.
learningOutcomes: State what SP 02 requires a permit drawing to show for an indoor pool and its barrier.
Describe what SP 02 says about recirculation and filtration designs at the permit stage.
Describe how a worker escalates an unpermitted or non-compliant barrier situation.
State the SP 01 start and finish time limits for swimming pool and barrier building work.

instruction.heading: Permit drawings
instruction.body: Victorian rule (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, Version 3, 26 September 2023). For an indoor pool, building permit drawings must show the barrier, the child-resistant doorsets and the direction the door swings. Recirculation and filtration designs must be given to the relevant building surveyor with the building permit application.

instruction.heading: Barrier standard
instruction.body: SP 02 names AS 1926.1-2012 as the barrier standard. Check the barrier against that standard, and report any shortfall rather than adjusting it on site.

instruction.heading: Stop, record and report
instruction.body: Workers do not move a barrier or precaution to get round a permit problem. They stop, record and report, and they do not put the fence back themselves.

instruction.heading: Time limits for pool and barrier work
instruction.body: Victorian rule (VBA Building Practice Note SP 01, Version 2.0, 27 April 2023). The building work has 12 months from the permit's issue date to begin, and six months from the start to finish. The note links these limits to regulations 53 and 54, which were not read for this lesson.

procedure: For an indoor pool, confirm the permit drawings show the barrier, any child-resistant doorsets and the door swing direction.
Note the permit's issue date and the planned start and finish dates, and check them against the SP 01 time limits.
At each visit, confirm precautions are in place and match the permit.
If a safeguard has been shifted or work goes on without a permit, halt, log the situation with date and time, and inform the builder and building surveyor.
Keep a written record of every stop and report.

workedExamples.situation: A worker arrives to find the site fence panels moved aside to give a truck access, and digging is continuing near the pool zone. A young child lives next door.
workedExamples.reasoning: The precaution has been changed, so it no longer matches the permit, and the digging endangers young children. Do not put the fence back yourself as a fix. Stop work in the affected area, record the position with photographs if permitted, and report to the builder and building surveyor immediately.

equipmentAndPpe: Copy of the permit and the approved plans
Hard hat, safety boots and high-visibility clothing

commonErrors.error: Moving a precaution to finish a job without reporting it.
commonErrors.prevention: Report any change to a precaution before anything else.

commonErrors.error: Starting pool work without checking the permit's issue date against the time limits.
commonErrors.prevention: Note the issue date and the planned start and finish dates before work begins.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A moved site fence or barrier is a drowning and injury hazard for small children. Stop, report, and do not correct it yourself.
Builder registration and owner-builder status are licence-type requirements in Victoria. This lesson does not grant registration.
Figures are Victorian. Permit drawing points come from SP 02 (26 September 2023); the time limits come from SP 01 (27 April 2023). This lesson does not cover permit stages or inspections.

qualityStandard: The permit drawings are kept on site and works are compared with them.
Every stop, report and direction is recorded with date, time and recipient.
documentationEvidence: Stop-work and defect report with date, time, photographs where permitted, and recipients
Record of any direction to fix and its written confirmation
summary: For an indoor pool, permit drawings must show the barrier, child-resistant doorsets and door swing direction.
Recirculation and filtration designs go to the building surveyor with the permit application.
Workers stop, record and report moved precautions and unpermitted work; they do not correct them themselves.
Pool and barrier building work has 12 months from the permit's issue date to begin and six months from the start to finish (SP 01, 27 April 2023).

knowledgeChecks.question: For an indoor pool, what must the building permit drawings show?
options: Only the pool depth and the pump size and the sun direction
The barrier, child-resistant doorsets and the direction the door swings
Only the builder's registration number and the builder's office address
The filter model and the water test results and the chemical brand

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker finds a site fence moved while digging continues near a pool. What is the correct action?
options: Move the fence back and continue while the digging goes on at the far end
Stop, record the position and report to the builder and building surveyor
Continue digging, since the builder is already on site and the fence is fixed later
Fill the excavation with water to protect it and leave the fence open for the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Under SP 02, to whom must recirculation and filtration designs be given with the building permit application?
options: No one, they are kept on site

sourceReferences: Victorian Building Authority, Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Version 3, 26 September 2023), indoor-pool permit drawing, barrier-standard and recirculation-design points; rights: user-held; reworded (no copying). Permit stages, inspections, time limits, final sign-off and stop-work powers were previously attributed to Practice Note 05-2018 and are not in SP 02.

Priority: official Victorian Building Authority source. It overrides other pool sources on the points it covers, for Victoria only. Dated: 26 September 2023 (Version 3); read through a summary tool on 2026-11-03. Victorian requirement. UNCONFIRMED for other states and territories, and the current edition of AS 1926.1 is UNCONFIRMED.

Victorian Building Authority, Building Practice Note SP 01, Swimming pool standards and safety requirements (Version 2.0, 27 April 2023), time-limit point only (regulations 53 and 54); rights: user-held; reworded (no copying). Read on 2026-11-03 through a summary tool, which returned short quoted fragments; the regulations themselves were not read.

UNCONFIRMED: current Building Regulations text (regulations 53 and 54 cited by SP 01, not read); builder and owner-builder registration rules in other states. Stop-work and reporting steps are practice guidance and are not stated in SP 02 or SP 01. Out of scope: Building Appeals Board appeals and performance-solution detail, which are design-stage matters for building surveyors.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3
officialReferences.covers: Victorian Building Authority Building Practice Note SP 02, Version 3, published 26 September 2023 (no review date shown). For indoor pools, the design drawings need to clearly show details of the barrier and child-resistant doorsets. Recirculation and filtration system designs are required to be provided to the relevant building surveyor. The page names AS 1926.1-2012 as the barrier standard. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 01, Swimming pool standards and safety requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 2.0
officialReferences.covers: Building Practice Note SP 01 (VBA), Version 2.0, published 27 April 2023, which supersedes Version 1.0 (28 June 2021). No review date is stated. Regulations 53 and 54 require building work for a swimming pool and barrier to commence within 12 months of the building permit's issue date and be completed within six months of commencement. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.
